[MUQATIL:29:56-63/r2] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | God reminds migrants that everyone dies and returns for judgment; faithful, righteous migrants receive eternal rooms with rivers, and those patient through migration trust God despite lacking money or livelihood in Medina.
[YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p638#2/r3] YAHYA-SALLAM, d. 200 · author | holds | The praised believers are those who are patient and rely on their Lord.
[IBNABIHATIM:v9p3078/r1] IBNABIHATIM, d. 327 · سعيد بن جبير | reports | Sa'id ibn Jubayr says the patient are those who persevere in obeying God's command.
[IBNABIHATIM:v9p3078/r2] IBNABIHATIM, d. 327 · عمر | reports | Umar says patience is of two kinds.
[IBNABIHATIM:v9p3078/r3] IBNABIHATIM, d. 327 · سعيد بن جبير | reports | Sa'id ibn Jubayr describes patience as the servant's acknowledgment.
[IBNABIHATIM:v9p3078/r4] IBNABIHATIM, d. 327 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn Abbas explains reliance on their Lord as hoping in no one besides Him.

[SULAMI:v2p119#2/r3] SULAMI, d. 412 · أبو بكر الوراق | reports | Patience means receiving affliction with a spacious heart.
[SULAMI:v2p119#2/r4] SULAMI, d. 412 · أبو سعيد الخراز | reports | Trust in God is agitation without stillness and stillness without agitation.
[SULAMI:v2p119#2/r5] SULAMI, d. 412 · الجريري | prefers | Al-Jurayri approves al-Kharrāz's paradoxical definition of trust in God as a good statement.
[THALABI:v7p288/r4] THALABI, d. 427 · author | holds | The believers praised here are those who patiently endure and rely on their Lord.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p553/r1] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · ابن عباس | reports | The migrants endured their religion, hunger, distress, and the loss of their property, children, and homes.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p553/r2] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | holds | To rely on God means to trust Him in the migration; Ibn ʿAbbās applies this to migrants who left their houses and property.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p553/r3] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · مقاتل | reports | Muqātil says migrants in Mecca worried they had no home or livelihood in Medina, so God admonished them to take heed.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p252#2/r1] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · author | holds | The patient endured hardships without abandoning their religion when distress struck; they rely on their Lord.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p323#3/r13] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | Patience and reliance on God gather all good, including patience in obedience and restraint from desires.
[TABRISI:29:58-60#2/r8] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | They endured hardship and harm without abandoning their religion, patiently performed demanding acts of worship, and relied on God in important affairs and migration.
[TABRISI:29:58-60/r8] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | reports | Alladhīna ṣabarū may be a genitive adjective for al-ʿāmilīn, with the praised subject omitted; alternatively, an implied iḍāfa makes the patient ones' reward the omitted subject.
[RAZI-FULL:v25p76#2/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Patience suits present hardship, while reliance suits future needs; the past cannot be recovered or altered.
[RAZI-FULL:v25p76#2/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Patience and reliance require knowledge of God and of the passing world: knowing worldly things are transient makes patience easier, while knowing God endures supports trust in His provision.
[RAZI-FULL:v25p76#2/r3] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | The surrounding exhortation suits two groups: those able to leave a place of harm rely on God and migrate, while those unable to leave endure harm and continue worshipping. | mentions 29:56
[BAYDAWI-FULL:29:57-60/r4] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | The patient endure pagan abuse, migration for religion, and other trials; they rely on their Lord alone.

[NASAFI-FULL:v3p263#6/r2] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | prefers | Connecting الذين to the previous verse as a modifier of العاملين is better than starting a new clause.
[NASAFI-FULL:v3p263#6/r3] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | They rely on God alone through all these hardships.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p364/r10] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | When Muslims in Mecca were ordered to migrate, they feared poverty as strangers without homes, property, or anyone to feed them; the animals' example reassures them that God provides even for creatures unable to stock provisions.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p364/r9] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The patient endure leaving their homelands, migration, and every hardship in obeying commands and avoiding prohibitions; patience and reliance on God comprise all good.
[SAMIN-DURR:29:59/r1] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | الذين صبروا allows genitive, accusative, or nominative, as in analogous constructions discussed earlier.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p292/r1] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | The patient remain steadfast in faith, migrate, leave enemies and even family and kin for God's sake, and trust their Lord in religious and worldly affairs.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p292/r2] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · أبو مالك الأشعري | reports | The Prophet says God prepared transparent chambers for those who feed others, speak well, fast, and pray while people sleep.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p292/r3] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | Trust in God applies in every circumstance, religious or worldly.
[BIQAI-FULL:v5p571/r10] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | They rely only on their Lord, renewing their trust in him in every matter, including provision after migration and struggle against enemies, rather than depending on family or homeland.
[BURSEVI:v6p353/r1] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | Those described as patient modify “the workers,” or are an accusative of praise; their patience covers persecution, migration's hardship, and other trials.
[BURSEVI:v6p353/r2] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | They rely only on God; strong faith loosens attachment to homeland, property, and provision, makes exile and home alike, and leaves God's reward sufficient.
[BURSEVI:v6p353/r3] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | reports | A hadith says that someone who flees with his religion even a short distance merits Paradise and companionship with Abraham and Muhammad; he merits Paradise for giving up home for religion and their company by following their migration and reviving their practice.
[BURSEVI:v6p353/r4] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | For the spiritual traveler, migration means leaving the land of social prestige and public acceptance for obscurity.
[BURSEVI:v6p353/r5] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · أبو سعيد الخراز | reports | When his reputation became so great that people competed to buy a melon that fell from his hand, he left; he was content to live where people called him an unbeliever and stoned him twice a day.
[BURSEVI:v6p353/r6] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · إبراهيم بن أدهم | reports | He said he had felt worldly joy only three times; in Antioch he went barefoot and bareheaded, welcomed being called a runaway slave, and told his self that if it had fled, it could now return peacefully.
[ALUSI-FULL:v21p11/r1] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | reports | Alladhina ṣabarū may modify the workers, be the predicate of an omitted subject, or be an accusative of praise.
[ALUSI-FULL:v21p11/r2] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | Their patience is through unbelievers' abuse, the hardships of migration, and other trials; they rely on God alone in all they do and leave undone.

[TABATABAI:29:59-60/r2] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | Believers should endure harm while religious life remains possible; if they cannot practice their religion in their land, they should migrate and endure the hardship that follows.
[TABATABAI:29:59-60/r3] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | Patience includes endurance in calamity, obedience, and resisting sin, though the Meccan context particularly means patience under persecution.
